key_insight: UPEBNL is a scalable causal Bayesian network framework that makes large-scale EHR-based cancer prescreening more interpretable by learning stable, evidence-traceable dependency structures.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help clinicians and researchers understand which EHR features contribute to cancer risk predictions while preserving strong prescreening performance.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR datasets for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine partial networks into a stable DAG
Global causal Bayesian network construction for interpretable evidence propagation
evidence_signal: In simulations, UPEBNL improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and ran up to 221.28-fold faster; in EHR prescreening it achieved AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: Because the causal structure is learned from observational EHR data, the resulting links are interpretable but not definitive proof of true causation and may need external validation.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
